nodes.body:
Greptile Summary

This PR adds persistence of inbound images to disk for the `chat.send` RPC path, bringing parity with the WhatsApp and Telegram handlers. Images sent via the webchat control UI (or native app clients) are now written to `~/.openclaw/media/inbound/` using the same `saveMediaBuffer` utility. Key design choices are well-motivated and correctly implemented: - **Fire-and-forget via `setImmediate`** correctly defers disk I/O without blocking the `"started"` acknowledgement sent to the caller. - The **`!isAcpBridgeClient` gate** correctly excludes ACP/IDE screenshot flows, which handle persistence upstream. - The code only runs **after** send-policy, stop-command, and dedupe checks, so only accepted requests trigger writes. One limitation worth noting: as explicitly called out in the in-code `NOTE`, the persisted file paths are not wired back into the session transcript. This means images saved here still cannot survive session compaction by reference — that is explicitly deferred as a follow-up. Reviewers should be aware this PR solves the "images never hit disk at all" problem, not the full compaction-survival story.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- This PR is safe to merge — the change is additive, well-scoped, and correctly uses an established utility with appropriate error handling. - The logic is straightforward and mirrors the existing WhatsApp/Telegram pattern. Fire-and-forget is correctly implemented via `setImmediate` with `.catch` guards. The `isAcpBridgeClient` gate is correct. The one point preventing a 5 is the acknowledged gap: persisted paths are not captured back into the session transcript, so the compaction-survival story remains incomplete — but this is explicitly documented as a follow-up and does not represent a regression. - No files require special attention. Greptile Summary

This PR adds fire-and-forget persistence of inbound webchat images to disk, bringing `chat.send` into parity with the WhatsApp/Telegram handlers that already call `saveMediaBuffer`. The change is well-scoped: it runs after all policy/dedup guards so only accepted messages write files, is gated to non-ACP clients to avoid double-persisting IDE screenshots, and uses `setImmediate` to ensure the `"started"` ack is never delayed by disk I/O. Key observations: - The implementation is correct — concurrent fire-and-forget saves are safe because each gets a unique UUID, and `server-maintenance.ts` already calls `cleanOldMedia` recursively (covering `inbound/`), so files do not accumulate indefinitely. - The PR description lists "Images lost after conversation compaction" as a fixed outcome, but the code comment itself acknowledges that saved file paths are **not** wired into the session transcript — that is deferred as a follow-up. The compaction-survival benefit is therefore not yet realized by this change. - The warning log label `"webchat:"` is misleading since the code path now covers all non-ACP clients (native iOS/Android/macOS apps and control UI), not just webchat.

Confidence Score: 4/5

- Safe to merge — the change is additive, well-guarded, and failure is non-blocking. - The logic is correct and follows existing patterns used by WhatsApp/Telegram handlers. No new dependencies are introduced, error handling is in place, and the fire-and-forget pattern cannot affect the response path. The only issue is a misleading log label. - No files require special attention beyond the minor log label fix in `src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts`.
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown This is a comment left during a code review. Path: src/gateway/server-methods/chat.ts Line: 1265-1268 Comment: **Misleading log label for non-webchat clients** The comment block above explicitly states this code path handles webchat, native app (iOS/Android/macOS), and control UI clients. However the warning message is hard-coded with a `"webchat:"` prefix. If a native iOS or macOS app user's image fails to save, the emitted log will read `"webchat: failed to persist inbound image..."`, which misdirects anyone debugging the failure. ```suggestion context.logGateway.warn( `chat.send: failed to persist inbound image (${img.mimeType}): ${formatForLog(err)}`, ); ``` How can I resolve this? If you propose a fix, please make it concise. `````
